# 2005 F-350 6.0L: synchronized HS-CAN + FORScan capture, 2026-10-25

**Inputs:** `2026-10-25_sync_can0.log` (candump -L, can0 listen-only 500k, OBD 6/14, 10:01:46.973–10:06:18.731 PDT, 271.8 s, 210 170 frames) and `2026-10-25_sync_forscan.csv` (FORScan 2.3.71, play click 10:00:36 PDT, 390.8 s). Truck parked the whole time: key on/engine off, crank, idle, two free-rev blips (peaks 2066 rpm and 2111 rpm), idle.
**Outputs:** `../../dbc/ford_2005_superduty_pcm_hscan.dbc` (now generated by `../../dbc/tools/gen_2005_pcm_dbc.py`), `2026-10-25_signal-finder/` (report + draft DBC), `2026-10-25_sync_plot.png`, scripts in `../../analysis/2026-10-25-sync/`.
All times below are seconds after the FORScan play click (CSV t=0 = epoch 1792947636.274 = 10:00:36.274 PDT).

## 1. Alignment check (`--ref-offset 1792947636.274`)
- The offset equals the first CAN frame (1792947706.973) minus 70.7 s, i.e. Hermes's value. The CAN log covers t = 70.70–342.46 s.
- **Crank:** FORScan RPM first leaves 0 at 100.90 s. On the bus, 0x201 RPM leaves 0 at 100.73 s and the first non-zero DID 0x1165 reply is at 101.13 s.
- **Blips:** CSV peaks at 259.118 s / 277.831 s. Bus 0x201 peaks at 259.13 s / 277.77 s. The DID 0x1165 replies peak at 258.93 s / 277.64 s, and those replies carry exactly the CSV peak values (2065.75 → CSV 2066; 2111.25 → CSV 2111).
- **Lag scan:** CSV RPM vs 0x201 RPM gives its best R² (0.9988) when the CSV is read 0.20 s later than the bus. Every FORScan column vs its own 7E8 DID gives the same +0.20 s. So **the offset is right to within ~0.2 s, and FORScan's timestamps trail the bus by ~0.19 s.** That's because FORScan linearly interpolates every column onto a shared ~32 ms grid (RPM steps 13, 25, 38, … at crank). A truly exact offset would be ~1792947636.08, but either value works with nearest-previous resampling.
- **Better reference:** FORScan polled over CAN, so its Mode 22 requests and replies (0x7E0/0x7E8) are in the same candump on the same clock. signal-finder decodes them (8480 replies, 0 negative, all single-frame). The DID replies are the cleaner reference; the CSV fits top out around R² 0.995.

## 2. FORScan PID ↔ PCM DID map (7E8, Mode 22)
Each DID was matched against the CSV column FORScan decoded from it. These formulas are now in `tools/signal-finder/sigfind/pid_table.py` `MODE22`.

| DID | FORScan PID | Formula | Match |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x1165 | RPM | (256A+B)/4 rpm | R² 1.0000 |
| 0x1446 | ICP | (256A+B)×1000/256 kPa (= /256 MPa) | R² 1.0000 |
| 0x1434 | IPR | A×100/256 % | R² 1.0000 |
| 0x1440 | MAP | (256A+B)/4 kPa | R² 0.9999 |
| 0x1172 | VPWR | A/16 V | R² 1.0000 |
| 0x1310 | EOT | (256A+B)/100 − 40 °C | within FORScan's 1 °C rounding (max diff 0.5) |
| 0x1139 | ECT | (2A − 32)/1.8 °C (2 °F/count) | R² 0.9986 (FORScan rounds to 1 °C) |
| 0x1123 | IAT | same as ECT (assumed) | only 3 values (19–21 °C): weak |
| 0x09CE / 0x09CF / 0x09D0 | FICM_VPWR / LPWR / MPWR | (256A+B)/256 V | R² 1.0000 (MPWR only 3 values) |
| 0x11C1 (2 B), 0x1667 (1 B) | probably VSS and GPL | – | constant 0 while parked, unconfirmed |

The glow plug lamp (GPL) was "Off" for the whole CSV, including key-on at 19 °C, so it can't be correlated.

The translator's b0-1 ×1.009 worked only because the flag is clear while running. |

### Requested checks
- **0x420 b0 = ECT °C + 40: CONFIRMED** (high, within the 19–39 °C seen). The old "medium" lead (0x74 = 76 °C) is consistent.
- **0x430 b1: NOT battery voltage (rejected).** ×0.125 gives 11.3 V KOEO against a real 12.0 V, and R² vs VPWR is only 0.39.
  - During the crank, VPWR fell 12.0 → 10.1 V while b1 only went 90 → 88.
  - When the engine fired, b1 jumped to 106–107 and decayed to ~94 within ~2 s.
  - Range 87–112. No reference fits it (best R² < 0.6 against all 11 PIDs, any bit field 1–16 bits). **Meaning unknown.** The start spike looks pressure-like (oil pressure?), but that's unproven.
- **RPM:** found, 0x201 (high). 0x225 b2-3 is a second RPM-like value.
- **VSS: not testable.** The truck was parked (FORScan VSS 0, DID 0x11C1 0). The translator's 0x201 b4-5 was 0 throughout, which is consistent but unconfirmed.
- **MAP:** only as boost in 0x200 b7 (medium). No absolute-MAP field found.
- **EOT: not found.** The only fields that correlate are ECT's (0x420 b0), and EOT barely moved (19–31 °C), so this is weak.
- **ICP: not found.** Best: 0x106 b0.hi (enum, R² 0.81–0.85), 0x225 b2-3 (0.89, just RPM), 0x200 b1 (0.82 CSV / 0.32 DID).
- **IPR: not found.** Best R² 0.63.
- **IAT: not found.** Only 3 values (weak).
- **VPWR: not found.** Best R² 0.69.
- **FICM V/L/M PWR: not found.** These barely moved (FICM_MPWR 53.5–54.5 V, 3 values; L/V 11–13.5 V, 6 values), so this is weak.
- **Glow plug lamp: not testable.** It was Off throughout.
- I searched every bit field of 1–16 bits (BE and LE) in the variable IDs against each DID. Nothing new passed R² 0.95 beyond RPM and ECT.

### What changes in 0x200 / 0x201 / 0x225 with the engine running
Medians KOEO → idle → blip.
- **0x200**
  - b0: 02 throughout. 03 for ~90 ms at start, 01 at blip ends.
  - b1: 0 → ~96 → up to 255.
  - b2: 01 → 04 → 03/01.
  - b3: 157 → busy.
  - b4: 03 → 03 → 04.
  - b5: 177 → ~112–133 → up to 253.
  - b6: always 0.
  - b7: boost.
- **0x201**
  - b0: low nibble + b1 = RPM; b0.7 = crank.
  - b2-3: 0x3FFF → ~0x4000 ± 90 (engine acceleration).
  - b4-5: 0 (parked).
  - b6: 0 → 0 → ~30 (pedal-like).
  - b7: 0x80, dipping to 109–127 in blips.
- **0x225**
  - b0-1: 00 FF constant.
  - b2-3: 0 → RPM-like.
  - b4-6: 0.
  - b7: 61 → 60–63 → spikes to 88 and 108 in the blips. Those spikes peak *before* the RPM peak and decay in 2–3 s.
  - The translator feeds b7 to the cluster as trans temp. It reads 61 cold (= 21 °C if −40, near ambient), but **no fluid temperature can move 46 counts in a second**. Trans temp is doubtful and this looks load-related. Trans temp wasn't logged, so it isn't settled.

## 4. Caveats
- **Ground jumper not confirmed** for this session: the USB2CAN-X2 may have had no common ground with the truck. The adapter logged a 0 TX count, and timing and payloads look clean (no stray IDs, steady periods), but treat it as unverified.
- The CAN file starts 70.7 s after the CSV. The 60 s key-on/engine-off stretch is only in the CSV, and the first candump's head was lost.
- Everything happened parked and cold (ECT 19–42 °C). Speed, gear, trans temp, hot temperatures and real boost under load are all unexercised.
- **Weak references** (few distinct values): ECT for the CAN overlap (21 values), EOT (13), IAT (3), FICM_MPWR (3), FICM L/V (6), GPL (1), VSS (1). Any "match" or "not found" for these is only a hint.
- There was one crank event, so every flag above is a single observation.
- FORScan's CSV is interpolated and trails the bus by ~0.19 s, so prefer the DID replies as the reference.
- Correlation can't tell "same signal" from "related signal" (e.g. 0x225 b2-3 vs RPM, 0x200 b7 vs MAP).

## 5. Next capture to close the gaps
- A **drive** with FORScan polling VSS (0x11C1?) and trans temp, plus pedal position.
- A hot idle to stretch the ECT and EOT ranges.
- A loaded pull for real boost and ICP.
- Confirm the ground jumper.
